input.quote: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Commencing on the later of (i) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Binimetinib Product in the Ono Territory, or (ii) [ * ] of the First Commercial Sale of the Encorafenib Product in the Ono Territory, Ono shall have the right to terminate this Agreement, for any reasons by giving [ * ] advance written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination.
input.rationale: Section 13.2 gives Ono (our side) an at-will exit, but it does not arise until the later of two redacted periods measured from First Commercial Sale of each Product, so for a multi-year stretch of a term running to expiry of the Secondary Royalty Term (13.1) we have no convenience right at all - walk-away territory under this rule - the notice period is redacted rather than fixed at 30 days, and no refund of prepaid amounts is provided. Array's side is acceptable: across the whole of Article 13 (13.1-13.5) Array's only exits are for cause (13.3 material breach, 13.4 bankruptcy), the 13.5 Safety/Efficacy terminations run to Ono alone, and Section 8.2 is a competing-product trigger, so Array has no convenience right during the committed term. Operation 1 makes the smallest change on our side: it deletes the delayed commencement, gives Ono an express right to terminate for convenience at any time on thirty (30) days' prior written notice, and adds the pro-rata refund, retaining the heading, the for-any-reasons language and the rationale-with-notice condition. On the verifier's diligence point, the only retained non-refundability language is the Section 6.1 upfront licence fee sentence; operation 2 carves Section 13.2 out of it so the refund is not contradicted, rather than adding a broad notwithstanding override. All other termination and wind-down mechanics are untouched.

mappings.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
mappings.quote: This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and, unless terminated earlier pursuant to this Article 13, shall continue in full force and effect

proposal.summary: Ono may terminate for convenience at any time on 30 days' notice with pro-rata refund; conform Section 6.1 non-refundability.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our position is that we must be able to terminate for convenience on 30 days' notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid amounts. We have deleted the delayed start tied to First Commercial Sale, made 13.2 an express termination for convenience exercisable at any time on thirty (30) days' prior written notice with a pro-rata refund, and carved Section 13.2 out of the Section 6.1 non-refundability sentence so the two provisions read together. Array retains no convenience exit under Article 13; we can discuss 60-90 days' notice as a fallback.

ops.newText: 13.2 Termination by Ono without Cause. Ono may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time, for any reasons, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Array which shall be accompanied by the rationale for such termination, in which case Array shall refund on a pro rata basis any prepaid fees or other amounts prepaid by Ono for the period after the effective date of such termination.
